encounters.cc: Routine follow-up of his HIV infection

lines: Routine follow-up of his HIV infection
He was diagnosed 2 years ago after presenting with chronic diarrhea, oral thrush, and progressive weight loss.
At the time of diagnosis, his CD4 count was significantly reduced, and his viral load was high.
He was started on combination antiretroviral therapy.
He has adhered closely to his regimen and reports that his energy levels have improved, his weight has stabilized, and he has not had any further opportunistic infections.
Today, he reports no new complaints.
- Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) infection with AIDS (CD4 <200)
He takes three antiretroviral agents, including raltegravir.
- Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate-emtricitabine 300-200 mg PO daily
- Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole DS 1 tablet PO daily (PCP prophylaxis)
He does not smoke, drinks alcohol only socially, and works as a graphic designer.
He denies fever, chills, cough, chest pain, abdominal pain, or neuropathic symptoms.
He has had no skin rashes and no medication-related gastrointestinal upset.
On examination, he is afebrile, blood pressure is normal, and BMI is within the healthy range.
The rest of his physical exam is unremarkable.
His most recent labs show an undetectable viral load and a steadily increasing CD4 count.

encounters.cc: 3-month history of progressive, painless skin lesions

lines: 3-month history of progressive, painless skin lesions
This 39-year-old male with HIV/AIDS and prior intravenous drug use returns to Dermatology for evaluation of progressive skin lesions following his January Infectious Diseases encounter.
He reports no fever, weight loss, or night sweats.
- Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) infection with AIDS (CD4 <200)
- Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate-emtricitabine 300-200 mg PO daily
- Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole DS 1 tablet PO daily (PCP prophylaxis)
His medical history is significant for intravenous drug use and unprotected sexual encounters with multiple partners.
He has not been in for a medical check-up for several years.
His temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), blood pressure is 125/78 mmHg, and heart rate is 78 beats per minute.
On examination, you note multiple, non-blanching, violaceous papules and plaques on his lower extremities and oral mucosa.

encounters.cc: Multiple skin lesions increasing in size over 4 months

lines: Multiple skin lesions increasing in size over 4 months
The 40-year-old male with HIV/AIDS (CD4 <200) and history of Kaposi sarcoma returns to Dermatology six months after his prior evaluation.
He presents with multiple skin lesions that have been gradually increasing in size over the past 4 months.
He reports mild tenderness in some areas and intermittent swelling of his lower legs.
He has had unintentional weight loss and intermittent low-grade fevers over the past 2 months.
He denies recent travel, animal exposures, or trauma to the affected areas.
- Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) infection with AIDS (CD4 <200)
His past medical history is notable for being seropositive for HIV for the past 8 years, and he has been intermittently nonadherent to his antiretroviral regimen.
- Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate-emtricitabine 300-200 mg PO daily
- Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole DS 1 tablet PO daily (PCP prophylaxis)
Physical examination reveals several violaceous, raised plaques and nodules over the lower extremities and oral mucosa.
No palpable lymphadenopathy is appreciated, and cardiopulmonary examination is unremarkable.
Laboratory studies reveal a CD4+ T-lymphocyte count of 84/mm³.
A punch biopsy of one of the cutaneous lesions is performed.

encounters.cc: Multiple violaceous lesions on his hard palate and lower extremities

lines: Multiple violaceous lesions on his hard palate and lower extremities
He returns for follow-up of progressive KS.
He also reports a chronic, nonproductive cough and several weeks of weight loss and night sweats.
- Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) infection with AIDS (CD4 <200)
His past medical history is significant for intravenous drug use and recurrent bacterial pneumonia.
- Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate-emtricitabine 300-200 mg PO daily
- Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole DS 1 tablet PO daily (PCP prophylaxis)
On physical exam, there are multiple reddish-purple, non-blanching papules on the skin and oral mucosa.
A chest CT reveals bilateral perihilar infiltrates and small pleural effusions.
A skin biopsy shows spindle-shaped cells, neovascularization, and extravasated red blood cells.

lines: Worsening shortness of breath, a nonproductive cough, and low-grade fever

The patient is a 41-year-old male with HIV/AIDS, prior Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, and Kaposi sarcoma, who presents to the emergency department with worsening shortness of breath, a nonproductive cough, and low-grade fever for the past 9 days.
He has difficulty climbing stairs and reports night sweats and fatigue.
- Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) infection with AIDS (CD4 <200)
His past medical history is significant for intravenous drug use and untreated HIV.
He has not seen a physician in several years and is.
- Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate-emtricitabine 300-200 mg PO daily
- Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole DS 1 tablet PO daily (PCP prophylaxis)
On exam, he is afebrile but tachypneic with a respiratory rate of 28/min and an oxygen saturation of 91% on room air.
Lung auscultation reveals faint bilateral crackles.
Laboratory testing reveals an absolute CD4 count of 82/mm³.
He is admitted for further management.

encounters.cc: Fever, left upper quadrant abdominal pain, and shortness of breath

lines: Fever, left upper quadrant abdominal pain, and shortness of breath

This 41-year-old male with HIV/AIDS, history of Kaposi sarcoma, and prior Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia presents to the emergency department complaining of fever, left upper quadrant abdominal pain, and shortness of breath worsening over the past week.
He denies any recent trauma or travel.
- Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) infection with AIDS (CD4 <200)
- Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate-emtricitabine 300-200 mg PO daily
- Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole DS 1 tablet PO daily (PCP prophylaxis)
On examination, his temperature is 38.9°C (102°F), heart rate is 110 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 22 breaths per minute, and blood pressure is 130/85 mmHg.
He appears diaphoretic and in distress.
Palpation of the abdomen reveals tenderness in the left upper quadrant with a palpable mass.
Auscultation of the chest reveals decreased breath sounds at the left base.
A chest X-ray shows a left pleural effusion.
An abdominal ultrasound reveals a complex, hypoechoic lesion within the spleen.

- Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) infection with AIDS (CD4 <200)
